lots.title: (1) Alistair Walker Infrequent Flyers Invergordon 35 Year Old Single Malt Scotch Whisky, Highlands, 43% ABV (GB)
lots.what_it_really_is: Alistair Walker Whisky Co. Infrequent Flyers, AWW Co. Release No. 123: Invergordon single grain Scotch whisky, distilled 1988 (roundel reads Distilled 1st Feb 1988), bottled Aug 2023, aged 35 years, cask 804138, dark rum barrel, dark rum finish, 273 bottles, 70cl, 43.0% vol, with tube.

Title omits 1988 vintage, Aug 2023 bottling, cask 804138, dark rum finish, 273-bottle out-turn and release no. 123. Real omission and a real error, but a 2023 grain bottling that retailed at about GBP 144 has modest value, so the effect is uncertain.

Roundel: 'AGED 35 YEARS', 'Distilled 1st Feb 19?8' (third digit soft but consistent with 1988), 'Bottled Aug 2023'. 386093_2: back label 'Single Grain Scotch Whisky', owner's story, glass print '15:59 14.08.23'. 386093_3: black foil over cap creased and torn at one side; fill sits at the base of the neck/top of shoulder, normal for a 2023 bottle. Tube visible behind the bottle (matches GB).

lots.title: (1) White Horse Cellar 'Appointment to Her Majesty the Queen' The Old Blend Scotch Whisky, Scotland, Circa. 1960's
lots.what_it_really_is: The Old Blend Scotch Whisky of the White Horse Cellar, White Horse Distillers Ltd, Lagavulin Distillery, Island of Islay and Glenlivet District, Glasgow and London; Queen's warrant (so 1952 or later); serial 'EU No 5489523'; 'Aged in wood'; 'Marca Registrada'; spring cap foil with pull tab; no size or strength on either label. Best dated 1950s to early 1960s.
lots.what_the_title_misses: Nothing of value. The title already names White Horse Cellar, the Queen's warrant and The Old Blend. Lagavulin is named on every label of this type, and 'Marca Registrada' is a trade-mark line, not proof of a rarer export edition. Webb's 'Circa 1960s' may be a few years late: the same label sold as 1952-58 and late 1950s-early 1960s, and the closest recent comp carries serial ES 3625190 against this bottle's EU 5489523.
lots.photo_evidence: My crops of 387001_1: 'THIS LABEL IS REGISTERED', 'BY APPOINTMENT TO HER MAJESTY THE QUEEN', 'SCOTCH WHISKY DISTILLERS', 'AGED IN WOOD', 'EU No 5489523', 'The Old Blend Scotch Whisky of the White Horse Cellar', 'Estab. 1742', 'Original Recipe 1746', 'Lagavulin Distillery, Island of Islay, and Glenlivet District', 'DISTILLED AND BOTTLED IN SCOTLAND', 'Distilled in Scotland and bottled in the United Kingdom under government supervision', 'PRINTED IN SCOTLAND', vertical 'MARCA REGISTRADA'; capsule 'Horse Scotch Wh...', '...Glenlivet Dist...'. No volume, proof or ABV anywhere. 387001_2: back label 'We guarantee White Horse to be very old pure blended Scotch Whisky ... Wallace and Clark's monthly analysis', small hole in the middle and a tear at the lower edge. 387001_3: fill high in the neck (good); pull tab lifted and capsule creased and split at the top. No box in any photo.
